title: 1965 AHSME Problem 29
statement: Of \(28\) students taking at least one subject the number taking Mathematics and English only equals the number taking Mathematics only. No student takes English only or History only, and six students take Mathematics and History, but no English. The number taking English and History only is five times the number taking all three subjects. If the number taking all three subjects is even and non-zero, the number taking English and Mathematics only is:

solutions.text:
Let \(t\) be the number taking all three and \(x\) the number taking Mathematics and English only, which also equals the Mathematics-only count. The disjoint-region total is \[x+x+6+5t+t=28,\] so \(x=11-3t.\) Since \(t\) is positive and even, \(t=2\) is the only value giving a nonnegative listed count, and \(x=5.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let \(t\) be the all-three count and \(x\) both the Math-only and Math-English-only count
